reviewMethod: Source text inspected during local development; concise paraphrases. No physical or CAD validation. Link-only references. Starter collection, not full historical coverage.

facts.body: The designer describes a two-stage continuous elevator with 60.8 inches of travel, mounted on the turret.
Cloudbreak used an elevator mounted on a rotating turret. The designer describes the ring, pinion drive and homing sensor.
A pneumatic prismatic arm extended the end effector beyond the drivebase.
The retrospective describes a two-roller ground cargo intake feeding the raised end effector.

robots.name: Stryke Force 2023
robots.locator: Opening post · mechanism and software feature lists

facts.body: The team lists a carbon-fibre single-stage elevator in its public release.
The released design has an arm attached to the elevator carriage, driven through a printed gearbox.
The team describes a custom swerve drive using printed Onyx parts.
The software feature list includes Photonvision AprilTag detection and automatic game-piece placement.

robots.name: Typhoon
robots.sourceTitle: 2910 · Typhoon CAD, code and technical binder release

facts.body: The team describes feeding at any turret orientation, with slower transfer at 90 and 270 degrees.
The team describes a dual-entry indexing system that transfers a note into the turret.
Typhoon had a climber; the team reported motor loading and unresolved reliability problems and recommended exploring alternative designs.
The team reported climber stalls and a burned motor. Its release explicitly cautions against copying that design without further investigation.

robots.name: Snoopy
robots.configuration: 2024 released robot · team control clarification June 2024

facts.body: The team reports a software-limited turret range of approximately 580 degrees, with wrap handling to avoid exceeding that range.
The team describes an elevator assembled using elements from several commercial elevator kits.
Goldfish used a modified Everybot-style climber, according to the CAD-release post.
The team describes a feeder-station intake using a ramp and indexer.
The feeder-station intake includes an indexer that pivots with the arm mechanism.
The combined arm mechanism pivots the intake and also dislodges algae.
The team reports extensive 3D printing in its coral-handling mechanism to simplify spare parts and replacement.
The team states that its shooter was fixed and used four 775 PRO motors.
Asked whether the robot used a turret, the team explicitly replied that the shooter was fixed. This documents absence of a shooter turret in the reveal configuration.
